analysis.title: Garrett - weekend prep - 8 Nov 2026
key_insights: Garrett calls the week's price action ugly. Index vol spiked, investors cut exposure, and volume and volatility data echo COVID, the GFC and Liberation Day. He says Thursday's stress was well below 2020 (VIX 70+), 2009 (VIX 60+) and 2025 (VIX 50+).

Stress that had been confined to single stocks and crowded positioning reached the index level. Garrett reads it as a violent positioning reset more than a systemic event, with more mechanical supply still to work through but exposures materially lower and index protection finally bought.

Trade idea: buy December upside call spreads across indices and sectors that look most washed out (long delta, flat vol, fade call skew). Names listed: DRAM, SOXX, SMH, EWY, MUTM, XLK, URA. Garrett expects more near-term technical weakness first.

New metric 'multiple surprise ratio' (MSR) compares an asset's 1-day % change with its 1-month implied volatility at t-1. SPX had its largest MSR in 19 years this week, NDX ranked top 2 and RTY top 5.

Prime brokerage: the global book was net sold, driven almost entirely by long selling. Single names were net sold for the 8th consecutive week, with the largest net selling in more than four months and a defensive rotation (sell tech and industrials, buy utilities, real estate and financials).

Global tech selling matched the largest net selling in GS's data set (in line with Oct 2026 and Sep 2024). Four of the five largest net-selling weeks in global technology stocks occurred in the last 5 months. TMT long/short funds were roughly flat on the year at Thursday's close, down from +24% in June.

The high touch desk was net better for sale on the week (-$6bn, mostly tech) but saw the first buy skew in semiconductors in 6+ sessions into Friday's close. The desk has sold $30bn of tech (TMT plus comm services) since the decline began, above July's $21bn.
Thursday's dollar notional traded was the largest regular-session volume ever, excluding opex and index rebalance sessions.

Systematic/CTA signals are negative in about 60% of global equity markets. GS calculates $28bn of SPX futures to sell in a week and $45bn in a month. CTAs have bought $33mm DV01 of bonds and are modelled to buy another $28mm next week and $78mm next month.

Clients took off protection after Wednesday's post-midterm-election rally, leaving them underhedged into Thursday. The jump in convexity has little precedent. Implied correlation spiked after a year of low realized correlation.

Garrett's Vol Panic Index hit 9.57 Thursday and closed the week at 9.2. Readings above 9 have historically been good buying opportunities. It is an equal-weighted basket of percentile ranks of VIX, SPX skew, SPX term structure and SPX 1m ATM implied vol.

On Friday investors chased VIX puts rather than index calls. The VIX put/call ratio closed near 1.5. Thursday was the third-largest ETF dollar notional day in history, at 33% of the consolidated tape versus a 28% average.

The desk likes shorting a diversified staples basket (GSXUSTAP). Staples trade at about 2x the 24-month forward multiple of the semiconductor index, and the valuation premium to SPX and the dividend yield both look overbought. The short on swap pays carry at current rates.
